Definition: from G206 and G1137; belonging to the extreme corner:--chief corner.
BiblicalUsage: Twice, both of Christ as the cornerstone. Paul says the church is built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone; Peter quotes Isaiah, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious. The word is the extreme corner — the stone that sets the angle for the whole building and holds it square.
TheologicalSignificance: Every stone in the building is measured from the corner stone. I believe that is why Paul and Peter both reach for it: Christ is not one stone among many, He is the stone that decides whether the whole house stands straight — and the house is us.
